titleEn: Wave a Flipper and Say Hello!

pages.text: "A boat!" Kkiruk called from the roof. A little boat puttered to the dock. An otter fisherman stepped off with a rod and bucket. Dad waved hello. Dari slipped behind him.
Dari wanted to greet him and see inside the bucket. But 'Hello' stuck in his throat. "What if he looks at me?" His tail fidgeted.
Dad and the fisherman laughed while tying ropes. Dari paced alone behind the lighthouse wall. Wanting to greet him but unable to, he nearly cried.
Dad found him. "Why hide here?" He pointed to the big lamp. "The lighthouse greets boats every night. It can't speak, so it waves its light."
Dad held Dari's flipper and waved it gently. "When words won't come, wave first. 'Hello' will follow." Dari practiced in his heart. Wave a flipper and say hello...
Dari took a big breath and moved toward the fisherman, a little at a time. Dad lifted a flipper behind him. The fisherman looked up and smiled.
Dari waved gently. Then the words came. "Wave a flipper... and hello!" His voice shook, but came out bravely. Dari slapped his tail. He had done it!
The fisherman beamed. "Hello! I'm here to fish." He tilted the bucket, showing leaping silver fish, and offered Dari one. "A gift for a friend with a lovely greeting."
Now Dari knew the steps. "One, meet their eyes! Two, wave a flipper! Three, say hello!" When the boat left that evening, Dari waved first. "Goodbye! Come again!"
Dad wrapped Dari's flipper between his own. "You did wonderfully!" Even when shy, a wave helped a greeting follow. "Wave a flipper and say hello!" The lamp flashed a greeting to the boat.
